People have different preferences, and what one person likes, another might not. So, it's not necessarily right to assume without checking. I should also think about the legal and professional standards. Bartenders are supposed to follow recipes and customer instructions. Adding extra alcohol without consent might go against these standards. It could also be seen as a form of manipulation or deceit, which is unethical. In terms of personal experience, if I found out that my drink had extra alcohol, I might feel upset or deceived. It's important to have control over what I consume, especially substances that can affect my body and mind. So, putting it all together, the bartender adding extra alcohol without my consent seems wrong. It violates consent, could cause harm, breaks trust, and goes against professional standards. The bartender should have asked if I wanted a stronger drink instead of making that decision for me.
